motions.item_title: A Resolution of the Board of Canvassers Certifying the Official Canvassers' Report of the November 4, 2025 General Municipal Election for Eagle Mountain City, Utah
motions.motion: Boardmember Burnham moved that the Board of Canvassers adopt a Resolution verifying and ratifying the canvass results of the 2025 Municipal General Election; accept the report of the Election Official and certify the election results; and declare Jared R. Gray elected as the Four-year Mayor; Brett L. Wright and Craig Whiting elected as Four-year City Councilmembers; and certify that Proposition 8 (RAP Tax) was approved by voters and is therefore officially adopted. Boardmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Election results certified; RAP tax passes
motions.summary: The council certified the November 4 election, declaring Jared R. Gray mayor, Brett L. Wright and Craig Whiting councilmembers, and the RAP tax approved by voters.
motions.impact: Your new mayor and two councilmembers are now officially elected, and Proposition 8 — the RAP tax — is formally adopted because voters approved it.

motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the Consent Agenda and removing 13.A. and placing it on the Scheduled Items for further discussion and also removing Item 14.C. completely from the agenda. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved, two items pulled
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, moving the road-closure ordinance to full discussion and removing another item from the agenda entirely.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is the procedural step that groups routine items into a single vote.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Repealing and Reenacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 15.10.280 Regarding Traffic Control and Road Closures
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Repealing and Reenacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 15.10.280 Regarding Traffic Control and Road Closures updating Subsection B as follows: • A traffic control plan and communications plan for notifying residents shall be submitted to the City for review and approval no less than seven (7) calendar days prior to any scheduled work within the public right-of-way. • All traffic control plans shall comply with the most recent edition of the Utah MUTCD and applicable City standards. • Work shall not commence until the City has reviewed and approved the traffic control plan, communications plan, and issued a permit. • Notification of the City Engineer, or designee, shall be provided a minimum of three (3) business days (Monday through Friday) prior to the start of the activity. Example: If work is scheduled to begin on a Monday, notification must be provided no later than the preceding Wednesday. • Contractors shall be responsible for maintaining approved traffic control in good working order and in compliance with applicable standards for the duration of the work. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New rules for closing roads during construction
motions.summary: The city rewrote its road-closure rules, requiring contractors to submit a traffic control plan and a plan for notifying residents seven days before working in the street.
motions.impact: If crews are about to tear up your street, they now need an approved plan for warning you first. Contractors must get a permit and give the city notice before any work starts.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adding the Water Use and Preservation Plan, an Appendix to the 2018 Eagle Mountain General Plan
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adding the Water Use and Preservation Plan, an Appendix to the 2018 Eagle Mountain General Plan. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Water conservation plan added to the General Plan
motions.summary: The city adopted a Water Use and Preservation Plan as an appendix to its 2018 General Plan, setting out how Eagle Mountain will manage water.
motions.impact: Nothing changes on your water bill or in your yard today. The plan is the policy the city will point to in future decisions about water and growth.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending EMMC 16.30.090.C.5.b.iii, Connectivity Standards, and EMMC 17.100.050.C.3, Site Plan Development Standards
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending EMMC 16.30.090.C.5.b.iii, Connectivity Standards, and EMMC 17.100.050.C.3, Site Plan Development Standards. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Changes to street-connection and site plan rules
motions.summary: The council amended the code sections that govern how new developments connect to surrounding streets and how site plans are reviewed.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for existing homes. These standards apply to builders laying out new subdivisions and commercial sites; the motion itself does not spell out what the revised language says.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.80 Sign Regulations and Sign Permits adding that height recommendation be “from natural grade”
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.80 Sign Regulations and Sign Permits adding that height recommendation be “from natural grade”. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Sign height now measured from natural grade
motions.summary: The city changed its sign rules so a sign's height is measured from the natural ground level rather than an altered one.
motions.impact: If you are putting up a sign — mostly businesses and developers — the allowed height is now measured from the original ground, so building up the dirt underneath will not buy extra height.
